note: Named acoustic conditions for the test chamber. Stage definitions are in docs/briefs/02-test-chamber.md. This file belongs to the user: tools read it and never rewrite it.

noise-3db.description: White noise, in-band SNR 3 dB. The reference point for sensitivity.

quiet-room.description: Phone held near the speaker in a quiet room.

living-room.description: Across a furnished room with some background noise. The case ROOM-1 exists for.

far-corner.description: Far side of the room: reverberant sound stronger than direct sound.

hall.description: Echoey hall. Known limit of the design; reported for information.

telephone-band.description: Narrow channel such as a phone call or a small AM radio.

clipped.description: Overdriven speaker or megaphone: 10x gain into hard clipping, with noise.

tone-on-grid.description: Steady whistle exactly on a tone frequency, 3x the amplitude of one tone.

tone-off-grid.description: Strong steady whistle between two tone frequencies. Known weak spot; reported for information.

speech-10db.description: Someone talking nearby, signal 10 dB above the speech.

speech-5db.description: Loud talking nearby, signal 5 dB above the speech.

street.description: Noisy outdoor setting: talking plus broadband noise.

rate-44100.description: Noise at 3 dB, run at 44.1 kHz.

rate-48000.description: Noise at 3 dB, run at 48 kHz.

video-then-room.description: Models the demo video path: compressed audio played on a laptop, phone across the desk (needs ffmpeg).

no-signal-noise.description: 60 s of white noise at RMS 0.1 with no frame in it. Nothing may be decoded.

no-signal-speech.description: 60 s of the synthetic speech-like interference at RMS 0.1 with no frame in it.

no-signal-tones.description: 60 s of six sinusoids (1047, 1319, 1568, 2093, 2637, 3136 Hz), each switched on and off at its own rate between 0.7 and 2 Hz, amplitude 0.05 each, plus white noise at RMS 0.005.
